issues.label: Housing & Rent
issues.description: NYC and NY State face a housing affordability crisis. Candidates differ on rent regulation, new development, and tenant protections.

issues.label: Climate & Energy
issues.description: NY's 2019 Climate Act sets ambitious targets. Debates center on implementation pace, costs, and the future of fossil fuels.

issues.label: Economy & Jobs
issues.description: From Wall Street bonuses to working-class wages, candidates debate taxes, business policy, and economic opportunity statewide.

issues.label: Public Safety & Crime
issues.description: Bail reform and policing remain contested. Candidates split on criminal justice reform vs. law enforcement investment.

issues.label: Education
issues.description: School funding, charter schools, and curriculum debates shape NY's education politics from NYC to rural districts.

issues.label: Healthcare
issues.description: Medicaid, single-payer proposals, and mental health access are central debates in Albany and Washington.

issues.label: Immigration
issues.description: NY's sanctuary policies and migrant shelter system have become flashpoints, especially in New York City.

issues.label: Infrastructure & Transit
issues.description: Congestion pricing, MTA funding, and upstate infrastructure investment are defining issues for NY's next leaders.
